newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money higher on rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money higher on rate increase.

text.p: *Central Bank lifts key rate in less than a week

Manila overnight money soared for the second consecutive session to an average of 11.53125 percent on Monday from 11.0625 after the 0.50 percentage-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 11.5 percent, dealers said.
The Central Bank said the increase, which was the second one in less than a week, was aimed at taming peso speculation. Banks had been wary over large outflows from stock market sales.
Done rates were at a higher band of 12.0/11.53125 percent, with 37 lenders and 23 borrowers. Volume swelled to 25.66 billion from 12.64 billion pesos.
The lifting of the Central Bank's key overnight rate forced banks to unload their old portfolio of low-interest bills.
"Everybody's selling," said a dealer. "Some are even selling at a loss."
"The rise in rates at the Treasury bill auction is going to be drastic this time," another said. The weekly T-bill auction is scheduled later today.
